question: Why is the absolute value function f(x) = |x| not differentiable at x = 0?
student_answer: Because mathematics is weird and numbers do strange things when they are near zero.

chunks.text: The function f(x) = |x| is not differentiable at x = 0 because the left derivative is -1 while the right derivative is +1. The corner point prevents a unique tangent line.
